speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the specific nature of your right leg weakness, how the unsteadiness affects your daily walking, and give me an example of the paranoid thoughts you are experiencing.

speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Subacute Combined Degeneration of the Spinal Cord due to Vitamin B12 Deficiency. The combination of rapidly progressive gait ataxia (unsteady gait, falls, right leg weakness) and significant cognitive decline (forgetfulness, paranoia) over weeks to months is a classic presentation. While other conditions like Hashimoto's Encephalopathy or Neurosyphilis are possible, B12 deficiency is the most critical to identify and treat immediately to prevent permanent neurological damage.

REQUEST TEST: Serum Vitamin B12 level, Methylmalonic acid (MMA), Homocysteine, and Complete Blood Count (CBC).
REQUEST IMAGES: T2-weighted MRI of the Cervical and Thoracic Spine.
